name: TOP Token
rootCause: The TOP Token governance system was built on Aragon DAO with a critically tiny total supply of only 16,384 TOP tokens, making it trivially inexpensive to seize majority control. The attacker acquired 8,192.000001 TOP — just over 50% of the total supply — and used this supermajority to pass a governance proposal that minted a large additional supply of TOP tokens directly to themselves. The newly minted tokens were then swapped through the TOP/WETH Balancer V1 BPool, draining 944.2 WETH (~$1.585M). The entire attack was executed in a single transaction via a dedicated exploit contract (0x25c6….729A21). Balancer V1 itself had no vulnerability; the pool was merely the exit venue where the attacker exchanged the minted tokens for liquid assets. This was a design-level failure: the governance mechanism placed no minimum token supply floor, no timelock, and no anti-dilution safeguard on minting proposals. Attack Tx: 0x967aa34c69b7775c718545c7f94d92e965eb5fc553c0f27f6f1a9c65c93ac156 Analysis: Phalcon on X
